text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High OTLP export error rate to Honeycomb detected for service=redwood-runtime in us-east-1. error_rate=37% over 2m. Pager duty triggered to rohan (oncall)

rohan (oncall): seeing it. paging telemetry team and eng-runtime. @sara @kim can you weigh in on whether this is an exporter-side backoff or local queue pressure?

sara: I’m on it. quick check: exporter logs show repeated HTTP 503s from honeycomb ingest endpoint and `connection reset by peer`.

kim: same here. telemetry agent logs: `otlp_exporter/export failed: server returned 503`. No obvious CPU/mem spikes on sidecars.

raj: any recent deploys to exporter or agent config?

mike: no deploys in the last hour. I pulled the telemetry agent image tag — unchanged.

rohan (oncall): ok, first-pass mitigation plan: 1) flip on local buffering mode (increase queue size) 2) reduce trace sampling slightly to avoid queue blowout 3) switch to fallback exporter (NewRelic) for critical customers if Honeycomb remains unhealthy. Doing steps 1-2 now.

sara: increasing buffer to 5k spans for runtime pools now via `telemetry.agent.config.queue_size=5000`

kim: lowering sampling from 100% -> 60% for debug traces via runtime feature flag `telemetry.sampling.global=0.6`

incident-bot: ACTION: rohan (oncall) assigned. Incident severity: Sev2. PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

rohan (oncall): starting to validate that buffer change applied across pods. Running: `kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=telemetry-agent -o wide` then `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /etc/agent/config` to confirm.

raj: I’m rolling a config to enable fallback exporter for critical routes. command: 
```
kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/redwood-runtime TELEMETRY_FALLBACK_EXPORTER=newrelic
```

mike: heads up — NewRelic license keys are in Vault, do we have permission to pull them from the control plane for this emergency?

amy-sre: yes, emergency read allowed. I'll push a short-lived token with scoped access for the rollout.

sara: Honeycomb status shows degraded ingest in `us-east-1`. https://status.honeycomb.io/incidents/abcdef — they report "partial ingestion failures" since 10:12 UTC.

kim: that aligns with our first error spike at 10:14. Looks like an upstream provider issue rather than local config.

rohan (oncall): customer impact check: Which customers use full-visibility traces (100% sampling) and are on hosted telemetry? @mike @raj - make a list.

mike: customers A, B, and C have 100% trace collection enabled. Customer D is on dedicated export route to Honeycomb but has fallback disabled.

raj: adding to that — Customers A/B are sensitive to trace gaps for debugging, but their request paths still have logs and metrics intact. This is trace-only.

rohan (oncall): communicate plan: 1) notify impacted customers that traces may be delayed/dropped due to Honeycomb ingest issues, 2) enable fallback exporter to NewRelic for Customer D and any other affected customers where consent exists, 3) revert sampling changes once ingest is healthy. I'll draft the message.

sara: FYI dropping traces will not impact inference responses. It will affect post-hoc debugging and perf dashboards that rely on spans.

kim: switching some pods to buffered-only mode completed on 12 pods. queue length stabilized for now.

raj: rolling env to enable fallback exporter for customer-D and customer-B. Patch applied. watch for `exporter= newrelic OK` logs.

mike: NewRelic connection successful for two pods. `otlp_exporter: handshake complete`

incident-bot: NOTE: runbook invoked: Telemetry Exporter Failure (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/telemetry-exporter-failure)

rohan (oncall): good. next: reduce alert noise — silencing the OTLP 5xx spike alerts for 30m while we stabilize.

amy-sre: done. silenced channel-level alerting for related rule.

sara: Honeycomb status just updated: "ingest spikes mitigated, backfill ongoing" but still partial. They estimate full recovery in ~30 minutes.

kim: seeing a steady drop in exporter error rate: now 4% over 2m, down from 37%.

rohan (oncall): updating PD incident with mitigation steps and customer impact. Draft: "Traces to Honeycomb experienced partial ingestion failures starting 10:12 UTC. We increased local buffering, reduced sampling to protect queues, and enabled a NewRelic fallback for impacted customers. No inference or user-facing request errors were observed. We will monitor and revert temporary config changes after Honeycomb recovery."

mike: copied. posting to status page for affected customers now.

raj: quick note: we should schedule a postmortem to understand whether our fallback path test coverage is sufficient and whether we can automate fallback based on exporter error rates.

rohan (oncall): agreed. tentatively scheduling postmortem at 1500 UTC today. Please add any logs/graphs to the incident thread.

sara: saved diagnostic bundle: `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1763004567/diag.tar.gz` includes exporter logs, kube events, and agent config snapshots.

kim: disabling the sampling reduction to avoid losing historical debug traces — reverting to 100% where buffer usage is back to normal. doing a staged rollback.

incident-bot: UPDATE: PD incident INC12345 status -> mitigated.

rohan (oncall): final check: error rate sustained <1% for 10m, buffers draining. Honeycomb shows backfilled traces. I am closing the active mitigation. We’ll keep monitoring for another 30m.

amy-sre: sending customer follow-up email draft for approval.

mike: good job team. action items: 1) automated fallback tests in CI, 2) add exporter health metric to routing playbooks, 3) runbook tweak to include immediate consent-check for customer-level fallback.

rohan (oncall): capturing action items in the incident ticket. will assign owners. Closing thread for active paging. If anything regresses, re-open with `/incident reopen INC12345`. :white_check_mark:
